What this article only briefly attests is that the daughter was declared capable of making her own decisions by a third party, to which her mother eventually complained.

It seems to me that the daughter's responsibility was distributed over several parties, over which the mother had little control. All these inividuals failed to meet the necessary competence to adequately attend the daughter's illness.

This, I've seen happen time and time again while I was a nurse for elderly people. They could live independently, except for some basic functions (eat, clothe, bathe, social conversation). TL;DR If you truly can't control a scientifically proven illness, you need a functioning support system. If that fails, change the support system! No excuse for being fat. Solve your problems, no matter what.

Norwegian Comedian's Documentary Hjernevask, "Brainwashing." Episode 1: The Gender Equality Paradox.

Harald Eia forces a dialogue between the influential social scientists in Norway's academic institutions and leading human biologists across the world. if you ever taken a class with one of these "social scientists" this is a mental orgasm for you. The other 6 episodes are also superb.

This documentary is a must see. After this documentary was broadcasted The Nordic Council of Ministers (a regional inter-governmental co-operation consisting of Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland) has decided to close down the NIKK Nordic Gender Institute. The NIKK had been the flagship of “Gender Theory”, providing the “scientific” basis for social and educational policies that, from the 1970s onward, had transformed the Nordic countries to become the most “gender sensitive” societies in the world.

The decision was made after the Norwegian State Television had broadcasted a television documentary called “Hjernevask” (the Norwegian word for “brainwash”) in which comedian Harald Eia exposed the hopelessly unscientific character of the NIKK.

Here is a list of the rest of the episodes with English subtitles.

Part 1 – ”The Gender Equality Paradox"

Part 2 – ”The Parental Effect”

Part 3 – ”Gay/straight”

Part 4 – ”Violence”

Part 5 – ”Sex”

Part 6 – ”Race” (password: hjernevask)

Part 7 – ”Nature or Nurture”

Yeah it really is a must see, Harald does a wonderful job in bringing up somethings that used to be so obvious (and still are if you talk to the "uneducated,") but now cause instant revulsion in so many.
